Recommended Highlights This Week

1. Singapore Night Festival 2026 begins – 21 August

2. POP TOY SHOW (PTS) Singapore – 21–23 August

3. Singapore Gallery Month 2026 – 15 August to 13 September

4. Lilytopia at Gardens by the Bay – opens 21 August

5. IVF World Sprint Championships – 17–31 August, Marina Bay

6. Assaggi – new contemporary Italian, Neil Road

7. Hungry Ghost Festival continues

Overall Summary

Singapore's after-dark calendar gets a major addition this week: the 17th edition of Singapore Night Festival opens on the 21st, transforming the Bras Basah.Bugis precinct into a free, after-dark playground themed around myths and legends, running three weekends into September. The same weekend brings POP TOY SHOW to Sands Expo for collectors, and Lilytopia opens at Gardens by the Bay for a more low-key floral option. On the water, the IVF World Sprint Championships turn Marina Bay into an outrigger canoe racing arena for the rest of the month – an easy, free spectacle for guests staying near the bay. On the Shangri-La side, Beng Hiang's nearly 48-year-old Hokkien recipes have found a new home at our own Garden Terrace, worth mentioning to guests who enjoy heritage local cuisine.

Events & Festivals

Singapore Night Festival 2026

Singapore's longest-running after-dark cultural festival returns for its 17th edition, transforming the Bras Basah.Bugis precinct into an immersive playground themed around “Myths and Legends.” Presented by HeritageSG, this year's edition spans four zones, including a brand-new Museum Zone centred on the National Museum of Singapore, home to the headline installation “Tales of Earth and Sea” – a large-scale projection mapping spectacle by Indonesian multimedia collective The Fox, The Folks. Opening week also features a Southeast Asian debut street theatre performance from Dutch group Close-Act Theatre. Most programmes are free.

Event Date: 21 August – 5 September 2026 (three weekends)

Location: Bras Basah.Bugis precinct, centred on the National Museum of Singapore

Admission: Free for most programmes

Best For: Families / Culture Seekers / Free Activities / Evening Outings

Concierge Recommendation: One of the best free things happening in Singapore all year – point every guest staying nearby toward this, regardless of their interests. Advise arriving early on opening weekend, since the National Museum zone will draw the biggest crowds.

POP TOY SHOW (PTS) Singapore

POP MART's flagship celebration of pop-culture toys and collectibles brings together global and Southeast Asian artists, brands and fans for exclusive product drops, fan-favourite activations and hands-on experiences – a bigger, ticketed follow-up to the free CRYBABY activation that's been running at Resorts World Sentosa.

Event Date: 21–23 August 2026

Time: Fri 12:00pm–10:00pm, Sat 11:00am–8:00pm, Sun 11:00am–8:00pm (confirm exact hours closer to the date)

Location: Sands Expo & Convention Centre, Level 1, Halls A–C

Best For: Collectors / Young Adults / Families

Concierge Recommendation: A natural next step for any guest who enjoyed the CRYBABY sculptures at RWS – mention this as the bigger, ticketed version of that same collector culture.

Singapore Gallery Month 2026

Presented by the Art Galleries Association Singapore (AGAS), this citywide celebration of contemporary art brings together more than 30 leading galleries across five weeks, with over 100 exhibitions, artist talks, guided tours, workshops and performances. This year's edition puts a deeper focus on the art of collecting, aimed at everyone from first-time buyers to seasoned collectors – including Collectors' Home Tours and one-on-one art advisory sessions for those on the Patron's Pass. Exhibition highlights include The Private Museum's “Shadows, Signals, and the Line,” FOST Gallery's “The Lie of the Land,” and ShanghART's “Taiki Sakpisit: 13 Nightmares.”

Event Date: 15 August – 13 September 2026

Location: Multiple galleries and partner venues islandwide, including Gillman Barracks, Tanjong Pagar Distripark, Bras Basah and Orchard Road – individual gallery hours vary

Admission: Free to visit galleries; some talks/tours and the Patron's Pass are ticketed

Website: agas.org.sg/sgm

Best For: Art Lovers / Culture Seekers / Something Different / Families (select workshops)

Concierge Recommendation: A good one to know even for guests who don't consider themselves “art people” – Gillman Barracks and Tanjong Pagar Distripark both make for an easy, low-commitment afternoon of gallery-hopping, and it runs long enough to recommend across several editions.

Attractions & Activities

Lilytopia

This is Gardens by the Bay's first-ever ancient Egypt-themed floral display, and it's worth knowing why it's not just “lilies you can find anywhere”: more than 7,000 lilies across 46 species and varieties fill the Flower Dome, anchored by a rare, genuinely significant bloom – the Egyptian Blue Lotus (Nymphaea caerulea), a sacred water lily that was so revered in ancient Egypt it was buried alongside pharaohs as a symbol of rebirth and the sun. It closes at night and reopens with the morning sun, the same cycle that made it a symbol of creation thousands of years ago. The display also marks the Flower Dome debut of two giant waterlily species, Victoria amazonica and Victoria cruziana – among the largest waterlilies in the world – grown from seed over 18 months by the Gardens’ own horticulture team. The centrepiece is a 4.5-metre-tall façade inspired by the Great Temple of Abu Simbel, with four colossal seated statues of Ramesses II, alongside figures of Egyptian deities including Hathor, Ra and Thoth.

Event Date: 21 August – 27 September 2026

Location: Flower Dome, Gardens by the Bay

Best For: Families / Photography / Garden Lovers

Concierge Recommendation: If a guest asks what's actually special about it, lead with the Egyptian Blue Lotus – a flower literally buried with pharaohs, not something they'll see in an ordinary garden. Also worth mentioning: Sensory Moments (29 August, 2:00pm–5:00pm, free with Flower Dome admission) lets guests watch the blue water lily open with the sun in real time.

IVF World Sprint Championships

Marina Bay turns into a world-class outrigger canoe racing arena as Singapore hosts the IVF World Sprint Championships, bringing international paddling teams to race against the city skyline.

Event Date: 17–31 August 2026

Location: Marina Bay

Admission: Free to view from the waterfront

Best For: Sports Fans / Free Activities / Waterfront Guests

Concierge Recommendation: An easy, free spectacle for guests staying near Marina Bay – no ticket needed, just point them toward the promenade during race times.

Restaurants & Bars

Assaggi

A new contemporary Italian restaurant from Chef Denis Lucchi – also the chef behind Michelin-starred Buona Terra – built around the philosophy that flavour matters more than picture-perfect presentation. The degustation-style menu focuses on honest, well-executed Italian cooking rather than fine-dining theatre.

Location: Neil Road

Opened: 10 August 2026

Pricing: Two tasting menus, The Signature Journey and The Pasta Journey (both from $88); 3-course lunch menu from $58

Best For: Couples / Italian Cuisine Fans / Business Lunch

Concierge Recommendation: A relatively accessible entry point to Chef Denis Lucchi's cooking without committing to the full Buona Terra experience – good for a business lunch or a lower-key dinner.

Special Mention: From Shangri-La's Restaurant Recommendation List

Two more picks this week from Shangri-La Singapore's own curated list of recommended restaurants across the city:

Buona Terra

Housed in a refurbished colonial bungalow on Scotts Road, Buona Terra has held a Michelin star continuously since 2019. Lombardy-born Chef Denis Lucchi – who also opened Assaggi this month – built the restaurant around Contemporary Italian cooking rooted in his own heritage, with sommelier Gabriele Rizzardi running an Italian-focused wine cellar. The entrance itself, flanked by an imposing wine display, sets the tone for an intimate, romantic dining room.

Current Promotion: None advertised.

Reservation Policy: No credit card required for standard bookings; call ahead for weekends and special occasions.

Hours: Lunch 12:00pm–3:00pm (Mon–Fri); Dinner 6:30pm–10:30pm (Mon–Sat), last order 9:15pm. Closed Sunday.

Contact: +65 6733 0209 / +65 9456 3147

Address: 29 Scotts Road, Singapore 228224

Dress Code: Smart and Elegant

Concierge Recommendation: A dependable, romantic choice for a special-occasion dinner – remind guests it's closed on Sundays, and that the same chef also opened the more casual Assaggi this month if they want a lower-key alternative.

CUT by Wolfgang Puck

The only Michelin-starred steakhouse in Singapore, and Wolfgang Puck's first Asian outpost, tucked into Marina Bay Sands. The menu takes a contemporary twist on the classic steak restaurant – premium meats, poultry and seafood sourced globally – paired with an international wine list running to more than 500 selections, one of the largest in the world.

Current Promotion: None advertised.

Reservation Policy: Reservations recommended; call or email to confirm current hours and booking policy.

Contact: +65 6688 8517

Address: Marina Bay Sands, 2 Bayfront Avenue, Suite B1-71, Singapore

Best For: Business Dinners / Steak Lovers / Special Occasions

Concierge Recommendation: A strong, dependable steakhouse recommendation for guests staying near Marina Bay – valet and self-parking are both available on site.

Hotel & Hospitality News

No new hotel or leadership announcements to report this week – all previously featured properties remain unchanged. Colleagues should continue monitoring for updates ahead of NoMad Singapore's late-2026 opening.

Transport & Operational Updates

Bras Basah.Bugis Crowds – Singapore Night Festival

Expect heavier foot traffic and some road/pedestrian management around the National Museum of Singapore and the wider Bras Basah.Bugis precinct on festival weekends (21–23, 28–30 August, and into September), as large crowds gather for the free evening programmes.

Marina Bay – IVF World Sprint Championships

Some waterfront walkways around Marina Bay may see temporary crowd management during race times through 31 August, as spectators gather to watch from the promenade. This does not affect road traffic.

Downtown Line Night Works

Downtown Line trains continue stopping earlier on Friday nights (last train around 11:30pm) and starting later on Saturday mornings (from 8:30am), until 5 September. Free shuttle buses run 5:00–8:30am Saturdays, connecting Bukit Panjang, Bugis, MacPherson and Expo stations.

Hungry Ghost Festival Continues

The Hungry Ghost Festival continues through 10 September, with Ghost Day itself on 27 August. Guests may continue to notice incense, joss paper offerings and getai performances around the island – see last edition for full background if the team needs a refresher.

Changi Airport Travel Advisory

Airport traffic remains elevated through the peak August travel period. Morning and weekend flights need extra buffer time for check-in, immigration and bag drop.

Looking Ahead

Singapore Night Festival – Remaining Weekends

The festival continues over the following two weekends (28–30 August, then into early September) – worth continuing to recommend in the next edition as well, since it runs well beyond this week.

GREEN-HOUSE Festival

Singapore's largest experiential sustainability festival returns for its fifth edition, 28–30 August 2026 at Temasek Shophouse, with its first-ever day-to-night format.

Additional Information

Concierge Notes

  • Singapore Night Festival is free and runs three weekends – a strong default recommendation for almost any guest with a free evening.

  • POP TOY SHOW is ticketed, unlike the free CRYBABY activation – don't assume guests know this distinction.

  • Buona Terra and Assaggi share the same chef (Denis Lucchi) – useful to know if a guest asks about the connection between the two.

  • CUT by Wolfgang Puck's exact current hours weren't independently verified this edition – confirm directly before booking.

Suggested Itineraries

Half Day — Free Evening in the City

Evening: Singapore Night Festival at Bras Basah.Bugis – start at the National Museum of Singapore for the Museum Zone, then wander the wider precinct for street performances and installations.

Tip: Arrive by 7pm on opening weekend to beat the crowds at the headline “Tales of Earth and Sea” projection.

Full Day — Gardens, Bay & Dinner

Morning: Gardens by the Bay – Flower Dome for Lilytopia.

Afternoon: Marina Bay waterfront to catch the IVF World Sprint Championships, then Marina Bay Sands SkyPark.

Evening: Dinner at CUT by Wolfgang Puck, right at Marina Bay Sands – no need to arrange separate transport.

Tip: Time the Gardens by the Bay visit for late morning to avoid the midday heat inside the (still air-conditioned) Flower Dome queues.

2 Days — Orchard & Civic District

Day 1

Morning: Orchard Road shopping. Afternoon: Lunch at Assaggi. Evening: Dinner at Buona Terra, then a nightcap at Hi Stranger on Neil Road (an easy walk from both).

Day 2

Morning to Evening: Bras Basah.Bugis for Singapore Night Festival, timed around POP TOY SHOW at Sands Expo if guests want to combine both.

Tip: Assaggi and Buona Terra share both a chef and a general Orchard-area location – easy to walk between the two if a guest wants to compare.
